text:
maria: quick flag — customer-onprem reported no audit events for ~45m after we applied the RBAC tweak for tenant eviction.

devon: which cluster/namespace? any errors in the audit-aggregator pods?

maria: cluster=cust-chi-02, ns=kube-system. I checked the aggregator pod; it accepted events but the sink push failed. snippet: `2026-03-10T03:12:14Z ERROR push: 403 forbidden from kms.decrypt`

ian_sec: 403 from kms usually means either the node/service-account lost access to the key or the proxy/firewall preventing KMS endpoint reachability. Did the RBAC change touch the service-account mapping for audit-shipper?

maria: we changed the tenant-evict ClusterRole to remove `secrets/get` for the exec-sidecar SA. That PR was small — didn't think it would touch the aggregator.

harry: fwiw we ran a KMS key rotation job at 03:04UTC for the onprem key-arn: redwood/priv/cust-chi-02. rotation logs show success but the job rotated the key alias which needs to be recognized by the aggregator's keystore

ops-bot: key-rotation-job/chi02-rot completed 03:04:07 UTC (status: success)

devon: can you paste the aggregator config? specifically the kms key ARN and the SA used to call kms?

maria: config excerpt:

```
auditSink:
  backend: s3
  kms_key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:999:alias/redwood/priv/cust-chi-02
  serviceAccount: audit-shipper-sa
  endpoint: https://s3.cust.onprem.local
```

maria: `kubectl -n kube-system get sa audit-shipper-sa -o yaml` looks fine; it still exists. But `kubectl get secret` in that namespace returned empty from the sidecar after the RBAC change.

ian_sec: that suggests the aggregator process lost permission to read the mounted secret containing KMS credentials (AWS creds or HSM token). If the secret can't be read the KMS client will fail with 403.

devon: another angle — our private deployments sometimes route egress through an egress-proxy VM with strict SNI rules. If the proxy only allows storage endpoints but not kms.amazonaws.com (or the onprem KMS host), you'll see the same behavior. Check conntrack on the egress-proxy.

sre-bot: quick checklist: 1) svc-account token mounted? 2) secret volume readable? 3) egress proxy logs for blocked TLS SNI? 4) KMS ACL includes SA/role?

maria: patch from logs: `permission denied: secret "redwood-kms-token" for user "system:serviceaccount:kube-system:audit-shipper-sa"` — looks like secret get was disallowed by the new ClusterRole rule.

ian_sec: ok root cause = RBAC removal. Short term options:
- rollback the RBAC change (fast)
- re-grant secret/get only to audit-shipper-sa (scoped)
- or switch aggregator to use node-identity (worse for isolation)

devon: short-term rollback + re-run audit-shipper push is safest. Also need to ensure audit events buffered on disk don't overflow. Command to check pod logs and stored files:

```
kubectl -n kube-system exec -it audit-agg-0 -- /bin/sh -c 'ls /var/log/audit/queued | wc -l && tail -n 200 /var/log/audit/shipper.log'
```

maria: ran that: queued=1843, shipper.log shows repeated `kms decrypt: access denied` from 03:12 -> 03:58

harry: I will reapply the old ClusterRole in 10m and coordinate with ops on the rotation alias fix. After rollback we should trigger a manual push: `kubectl -n kube-system exec audit-agg-0 -- /bin/sh -c '/usr/local/bin/shipper flush --force'`

devon: medium-term: add an integration test in the private-deploy CI that rotates a test key and verifies aggregator can still decrypt (synthetic audit event). Also alert on queued audit count > 1000.

ian_sec: isolation note: for Private deployments we accept that components may need scoped secret access (audit shipper SA can be granted read-only to a single secret). That preserves tenant eviction semantics while keeping least privilege. Avoid bundling audit shipper creds into tenant-scoped roles.

maria: question — will egress-proxy + strict netpol break the guarantee that audit logs are delivered even during tenant evictions? We need a documented failure mode.

devon: yes — if eviction path includes removing secret-get then audit shipping will fail. Failure modes: lost-to-disk (if disk persists) or permanent loss if eviction also removes pod volumes. For guarantee we need:
- backup: local buffered disk + retention policy across reboots
- control-plane fallback: aggregator can push to internal queue (message broker in-cluster) that is allowed by netpol even during eviction

sre-bot: proposal -> Add runbook: 1) RBAC change gating: any change affecting `secrets/get` must run a preflight that verifies audit-shipper SA still has access. 2) Add synthetic probe that rotates a test key weekly. 3) Add alert on `queued > 500` and `last_success > 30m`.

maria: agreed. I'll rollback now and follow up with a PR to add the preflight and alert. Thanks team :thumbsup:

harry: will also patch the rotation job to update aggregator keystore alias mapping (so rotation is transparent).

ian_sec: file a short postmortem (one-pager) linking the RBAC diff + rotation event; tag compliance for audit record. We should capture the exact timeline so customers' SLA questions are answerable.

maria: filing now — will include logs + commands. ping me if you want access to the scratch cluster for reproducing the netpol+rotation scenario.

ops-bot: jira RED-PRIV-527 created: "eviction RBAC preflight + audit-shipper resiliency" assigned maria, devon (priority: P1)

maria: closing the loop: rollback applied at 03:56 UTC, audit-shipper flush succeeded at 04:03 UTC, queued drained to 0 by 04:12 UTC. I'll post the PR link shortly.
